title: etet, sétáltat, simogat: Looking After a Pet

sections.title: Three verbs for caring for an animal
sections.content: *etet* ("to feed"), *sétáltat* ("to walk a dog") and *simogat* ("to stroke") all take an object. You know the pattern from A1: the *-t* on the object (*a macskát*) and the definite verb ending when the object has *a* or *az* (*etetem*, *simogatom*). Do not mix up *sétál* and *sétáltat*: *sétálok* means "I go for a walk", but *sétáltatom a kutyát* means "I take the dog for a walk".

I go for a walk with the dog in the park.

sections.content: *etet* is not *eszik*: *a macska eszik* means "the cat eats", but *etetem a macskát* means "I feed the cat". The animal is the object, and it takes the *-t*.
